</style><style data-tailwind-stylesheet="true"></style><div class="readme-tailwind"><h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="prerequisites"></div><div class="heading-text">Prerequisites</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Prerequisites" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#prerequisites"></a></h2>
<ul>
<li>Have an Optimizely Web Experimentation account.</li>
<li>Have an Optimizely Data Platform (ODP) account.</li>
<li><a target="_blank" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411731640973" label="Add the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet to your site" rel="noopener noreferrer">Add the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet to your site</a>.</li>
<li><a target="_blank" href="https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/optimizely-data-platform/docs/implement-the-odp-javascript-tag" label="Add the ODP snippet to your site">Add the ODP snippet to your site</a>.
<blockquote class="callout callout_warn" theme="🚧"><span class="callout-icon">🚧</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="important"></div><div class="heading-text">Important</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Important" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#important"></a></h3><p>The ODP snippet is optional if you select the <strong>Web • Visitor ID</strong> in step 7 below, or if you do not use ODP as your customer data platform (CDP) and are implementing the audience sync version of this integration.</p><p>If you add the ODP snippet to your site, it must be before the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet so that the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet can pull the ID that the ODP snippet generates.</p></blockquote>
</li>
<li>Have <a target="_blank" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/37582243690765-Build-real-time-audiences-in-ODP" label="real-time audiences" rel="noopener noreferrer">real-time audiences</a> configured in ODP.</li>
</ul>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="integration-considerations"></div><div class="heading-text">Integration considerations</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Integration considerations" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#integration-considerations"></a></h2>
<ul>
<li><strong>Third-party CDP</strong> — If you do not use ODP as your CDP, you still need an ODP account but do not have to implement the ODP snippet on your site. To configure the Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation integration using a third-party CDP, skip to <a target="_blank" href="#integrate-with-other-cdps" label="Integrate with other CDPs">Integrate with other CDPs</a>.</li>
<li><strong>ODP</strong> — If you use ODP as your CDP, continue to <a target="_self" href="#configure-real-time-segments-for-web-experimentation">Configure Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation</a>.</li>
</ul>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="configure-real-time-segments-for-web-experimentation"></div><div class="heading-text">Configure Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Configure Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#configure-real-time-segments-for-web-experimentation"></a></h2>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Go to <strong>Settings > Integrations > Real-Time Segments</strong> in Optimizely Web Experimentation.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="Real-Time Segments Integration" class="img  " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/b078a0f-real-time_segments_integration.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p>Toggle the integration status to <strong>On</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>You can find your API key in ODP</strong> to go to the <strong>APIs</strong> page in ODP.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Copy the <strong>KEY</strong> value in the <strong>Public</strong> and <strong>Private</strong> tabs on the <strong>APIs</strong> page in ODP.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="Copy API Keys" class="img  " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/e0c85b0-copy_keys.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p>Go back to Optimizely Web Experimentation and paste these values into the corresponding fields (<strong>ODP Public Key (required)</strong> and <strong>ODP Private Key (required)</strong>).</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="Paste API Keys" class="img  " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/5657ab2-Paste_keys.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select your region from the <strong>ODP Host (required)</strong> drop-down list.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select your desired <strong>User ID</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>ODP • VUID</strong> — The ID that ODP assigns to each customer cookie. This is the default ID for the integration.</li>
<li><strong>Web • Visitor ID</strong> — (Default) The ID that your Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet is using. Depending on your snippet settings, this is either the default Optimizely Web Experimentation visitor ID or <a target="_blank" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411652974477-Bring-your-own-visitor-ID-BYOID-" label="another ID of your choice" rel="noopener noreferrer">another ID of your choice</a>.
<blockquote class="callout callout_warn" theme="🚧"><span class="callout-icon">🚧</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="important-1"></div><div class="heading-text">Important</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Important" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#important-1"></a></h3><p>For help with selecting the <strong>User ID</strong>, see <a target="_blank" href="#select-your-user-id" label="Select your User ID">Select your User ID</a>.</p></blockquote>
</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p>Select your desired <strong>Confidence Level</strong> for the <strong>User ID</strong> you selected above:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Low confidence</strong> — Low confidence identifiers are unique to a device or browser and may resolve to multiple customers in certain situations. Select this option when there is a weak degree of confidence that your chosen <strong>User ID</strong> accurately represents a single customer.
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note"></a></h3><p><strong>Low confidence</strong> is the only option available if you select <strong>ODP • VUID</strong> for your <strong>User ID</strong>.</p></blockquote>
</li>
<li><strong>High confidence</strong> — High confidence identifiers are unique to an individual customer. Select this option only when you have a high degree of confidence that your chosen <strong>User ID</strong> accurately represents a single customer.
See <a target="_blank" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407767067149-Overview-of-customer-identity-and-resolution" label="Overview of customer identity and resolution" rel="noopener noreferrer">Overview of customer identity and resolution</a> for more information.</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong>.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="select-your-user-id"></div><div class="heading-text">Select your User ID</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Select your User ID" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#select-your-user-id"></a></h3>
<p>When deciding which <strong>User ID</strong> to select, consider the following requirements for each option:</p>
<p><strong>ODP • VUID</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>You must implement both the ODP and Optimizely Web Experimentation snippets on your site.</li>
<li>You must have the ODP snippet activated before the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet.</li>
<li>You cannot implement the ODP snippet asynchronously.</li>
<li>This is a low-confidence identifier.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Web • Visitor ID</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>You must implement the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet on your site.</li>
<li>Implementing the ODP snippet is optional. If you choose not to implement it, just implement the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet, then skip directly to <a target="_self" href="#use-odp-real-time-segments-in-your-optimizely-web-experimentation-experiments">Use ODP real-time segments in your Optimizely Web Experimentation experiments</a>.</li>
<li>You can keep your performance budget for your site lower by only implementing one snippet as opposed to implementing both.</li>
<li>You can select whether you want this to be a low-confidence or high-confidence identifier.</li>
</ul>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="integrate-with-other-cdps"></div><div class="heading-text">Integrate with other CDPs</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Integrate with other CDPs" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#integrate-with-other-cdps"></a></h2>
<blockquote class="callout callout_warn" theme="🚧"><span class="callout-icon">🚧</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="important-2"></div><div class="heading-text">Important</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Important" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#important-2"></a></h3><p>If you use ODP as your CDP, do not complete this section. Skip to <a target="_self" href="#use-odp-real-time-segments-in-your-optimizely-web-experimentation-experiments">Use ODP real-time segments in your Optimizely Web Experimentation experiments</a>.</p></blockquote>
<p>If you use a third-party CDP:</p>
<ol>
<li>Configure the <a target="_blank" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/19650895342349-CDP-audience-sync-environment" label="third-party CDP integration in ODP" rel="noopener noreferrer">third-party CDP integration in ODP</a>.</li>
<li>Go to <strong>Settings > Integrations > Real-Time Segments</strong> in Optimizely Web Experimentation.</li>
<li>Toggle the integration status to <strong>On</strong>.</li>
<li>Click <strong>You can find your API key in ODP</strong> to navigate to the <strong>APIs</strong> page in ODP.</li>
<li>Copy the <strong>KEY</strong> value in the <strong>Public</strong> and <strong>Private</strong> tabs on the <strong>APIs</strong> page in ODP.</li>
<li>Go back to Optimizely Web Experimentation and paste these values into the corresponding fields (<strong>ODP Public Key (required)</strong> and <strong>ODP Private Key (required)</strong>).</li>
<li>Select your region from the <strong>ODP Host (required)</strong> drop-down list.</li>
<li>Select the <strong>CDP Audience Sync Implementation</strong> checkbox.</li>
<li>Select an <strong>Identifier Type</strong>.
<blockquote class="callout callout_warn" theme="🚧"><span class="callout-icon">🚧</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="important-3"></div><div class="heading-text">Important</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Important" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#important-3"></a></h3><p>Select an identifier type that matches the identifier sent from your CDP to ODP to increase the likelihood of user bucketing. See <a target="_blank" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411652974477-Bring-your-own-visitor-ID-BYOID-#heading-2" label="the user documentation on identifier types" rel="noopener noreferrer">the user documentation on identifier types</a> for information.</p></blockquote>
</li>
<li>Enter the <strong>Identifier Name</strong>.</li>
</ol>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="use-odp-real-time-audiences-in-your-optimizely-web-experimentation-experiments"></div><div class="heading-text">Use ODP real-time audiences in your Optimizely Web Experimentation experiments</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Use ODP real-time audiences in your Optimizely Web Experimentation experiments" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#use-odp-real-time-audiences-in-your-optimizely-web-experimentation-experiments"></a></h2>
<p>Now you can build audiences in Optimizely Web Experimentation using ODP's <a target="_blank" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/37582243690765-Build-real-time-audiences-in-ODP" label="real-time audiences" rel="noopener noreferrer">real-time audiences</a>.</p>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-1"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-1"></a></h3><p>The audiences on the <strong>Customers > Audiences</strong> page in ODP are not available for use in this integration.</p></blockquote>
<h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="create-an-audience-using-odps-real-time-audiences"></div><div class="heading-text">Create an audience using ODP's real-time audiences</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Create an audience using ODP's real-time audiences" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#create-an-audience-using-odps-real-time-audiences"></a></h3>
<p>You can create and add an audience directly in your experiment (described below), or you can create the audience outside of the experiment (<a target="_blank" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/37582243690765-Build-real-time-audiences-in-ODP" label="using the audience builder" rel="noopener noreferrer">using the audience builder</a>) and add it to your experiment later.</p>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Go to <strong>Audiences</strong> in your experiment.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Create New Audience</strong>.</p>
<span aria-label="Expand image" class="img lightbox closed" role="button" tabindex="0"><span class="lightbox-inner"><img alt="Create New Audience" class="img  " height="auto" loading="lazy" src="https://files.readme.io/d97938c-10f0f4e-odp2-2.png" title="" width="auto"></span></span>
</li>
<li>
<p>Complete the <strong>Name</strong> (required) and <strong>Description</strong> (optional) fields.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Expand <strong>Real-Time Segments</strong> in the audience conditions options.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Drag and drop either <strong>Custom Segments</strong> to the <strong>Audience Conditions</strong> section.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Configure the audience as desired (the real-time segments from ODP display in the <strong>Select an audience</strong> drop-down list).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save Audience</strong>.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click <strong>Save</strong> on the <strong>Audiences</strong> page.</p>
</li>
</ol>
<blockquote class="callout callout_info" theme="📘"><span class="callout-icon">📘</span><h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="note-2"></div><div class="heading-text">Note</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Note" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#note-2"></a></h3><p>The Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet does not evaluate ODP real-time segment membership unless you add an audience that uses ODP real-time audiences to a live experiment that is being activated. Add the audience you create (using the steps above) to an experiment to see this integration function on a particular webpage.</p><p>If you check for a value that could change ODP real-time segment membership mid-session, a page needs to be activated for an experiment using an audience to force re-evaluation (as it normally would for any other audience condition). See <a target="_blank" href="https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4410289779853-How-the-Optimizely-snippet-works-Order-of-activation" label="order of activation" rel="noopener noreferrer">order of activation</a> for information.</p></blockquote>
<h2 class="heading heading-2 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="troubleshoot-the-integration"></div><div class="heading-text">Troubleshoot the integration</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Troubleshoot the integration" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#troubleshoot-the-integration"></a></h2>
<p>If you do not see the issue you are experiencing below, contact Optimizely Support.</p>
<h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="visitors-are-not-getting-bucketed-into-experiments"></div><div class="heading-text">Visitors are not getting bucketed into experiments</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Visitors are not getting bucketed into experiments" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#visitors-are-not-getting-bucketed-into-experiments"></a></h3>
<p><strong>API key daily request limit</strong></p>
<p>In rare cases, you may reach ODP's public API key daily request limit of 1 million. This prevents Web Experimentation from bucketing visitors into experiments that use Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation. Other experiments continue to work, and experiments using Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation resume the next day.</p>
<p>It is unlikely that hitting the ODP public API key daily request limit would cause a sample ratio mismatch (SRM). SRM is related to overall traffic allocation to experiments, not traffic distribution among variations.</p>
<p>If you reach the ODP public API key request limit and the API calls fail for the rest of the day, there may be a slight delay in reaching statistical significance. While the time to the conclusion of a test is driven by an accumulation of evidence, it is <em>mainly</em> driven by an accumulation of evidence where there is a consistent, compelling effect to be found. What impacts the speed to a conclusion is more about a thoughtfully designed experiment.</p>
<p><strong>ID not found</strong></p>
<p>You may see a message from ODP that it could not locate a visitor's ID to bucket them. This is not bad and is a possibility in the integration due to what is called a <a target="_blank" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_condition" label="race condition" rel="noopener noreferrer">race condition</a>.</p>
<p>When the snippet activates, it evaluates the URL targeting in the project. When the page's targeting conditions are passed, the page activates, and Optimizely Web Experimentation evaluates the experiments for that page and whether a visitor should be in the experiment, based on traffic allocation and audience conditions. If both audience and traffic conditions are passed, the experiment activates.</p>
<p>During bucketing, Optimizely Web Experimentation generates a random ID for the user and sets it as a cookie while activating the snippet. With Real-Time Segments, Optimizely Web Experimentation calls ODP to retrieve the segments for the visitor's ID. If the snippet asks for the ID before the ID has reached ODP, ODP may give an unrecognized ID response because sending data to ODP is slower than the snipper activation. This is called a race condition, where the end result differs based on the order in which concurrent logic is completed.</p>
<p>After receiving this response from ODP, Optimizely Web Experimentation does not attempt to finish bucketing for that experiment or campaign and moves to the next experience.</p>
<p><strong>Network request interception</strong></p>
<p>When an experiment targets Real-Time Segments from ODP, Web Experimentation uses the GraphQL API from ODP to fetch the visitor's RTS membership. As with any other third-party audience integrations, Web Experimentation waits for a response for a maximum of 2 seconds. If the API response does not return within 2 seconds, the audience is evaluated as false, and the visitor is not bucketed into the experiment.</p>
<p>On some websites, your JavaScript framework may intercept the network requests that Web Experimentation initiates. This interception adds overhead and can delay the network request and response, causing Web Experimentation to receive the response from ODP after 2 seconds.</p>
<p>To prevent this, Optimizely Support can enable sandboxing in the Web Experimentation project. This is a project-level setting not directly accessible to you. When enabled, the snippet adds an empty iframe to the <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter"><head></span></code> section of your website. The API requests to third-party audience integrations are then passed through that iframe, which should prevent them from being intercepted. This lets the responses get back to Web Experimentation in time to evaluate the audiences correctly.</p>
<p>To see if this issue is occurring, open <strong>Developer tools > Network</strong>. Filter the network logs for <strong>graphql</strong>, and select the <strong>Initiator</strong> tab. The initiator stack should show the snippet. If the stack shows another script, this indicates the request from the snippet was intercepted, and delays may occur. Contact the Support team for further investigation and possible enabling of the Sandboxing setting.</p>
<h3 class="heading heading-3 header-scroll"><div class="heading-anchor anchor waypoint" id="check-which-real-time-audiences-you-are-assigned-to-in-odp"></div><div class="heading-text">Check which real-time audiences you are assigned to in ODP</div><a aria-label="Skip link to Check which real-time audiences you are assigned to in ODP" class="heading-anchor-icon fa fa-regular fa-anchor" href="#check-which-real-time-audiences-you-are-assigned-to-in-odp"></a></h3>
<p>When Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation is enabled, Optimizely Web Experimentation makes a request to the ODP GraphQL API to retrieve the current visitor's assigned real-time audiences. To inspect the data returned by that call, open the developer console and check the value of this attribute:</p>
<div class="CodeTabs CodeTabs_initial theme-light"><div class="CodeTabs-toolbar"><button type="button" value="javascript">JavaScript</button></div><div class="CodeTabs-inner"><pre><button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-javascript theme-light" data-lang="javascript"><div class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter"><span class="cm-variable">window</span>[<span class="cm-string">"optimizely"</span>].<span class="cm-property">get</span>(<span class="cm-string">"visitor"</span>)[<span class="cm-string">'vendor.odp'</span>][<span class="cm-string">'audiences'</span>]</div></code></pre></div></div>
<p>The content of this array should be populated with any real-time segments to which you are currently assigned.</p>
<p>If you do not see any real-time audiences in the <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">odp.audiences[]</span></code> array, first check to see if you are a member of the <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">returning_visitors</span></code> real-time segment by navigating away from the page and returning to it. If you see yourself in the <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">returning_visitors</span></code> real-time audience on your second visit to the page, the problem could be that you do not belong to any other audiences, or those audiences have not been enabled for that page.</p>
<p>If, however, you are <em>not</em> in the <button aria-label="Copy Code" class="rdmd-code-copy fa"></button><code class="rdmd-code lang-undefined theme-light"><span class="cm-s-neo" data-testid="SyntaxHighlighter">returning_visitors</span></code> real-time segment, the ODP tracker may be disabled. This often happens when a visitor deletes their browser cookies mid-session. In this case, the ODP tracker needs to reacquire a tracking cookie before it can identify the user. If the ODP JavaScript snippet cannot find the cookie, ODP returns an empty array of audience memberships. You can reset the cookie by logging out and back into the site.</p></div></div></div><div align="center" class="Flex Flex_row " justify="between" style="--flex-gap: var(--md);"><div function initNewTabEnforcer() {
  const isExternal = (href) => {
    try {
      const u = new URL(href, location.href);
      return u.origin !== location.origin;
    } catch { return false; }
  };

  const hardenAnchor = (a) => {
    if (!a || !a.href) return;
    if (!isExternal(a.href)) return;
    if (a.dataset.allowIframe != null || a.classList?.contains('allow-iframe')) return;
    a.target = '_blank';
    a.rel = 'noopener noreferrer';
    a.__newTabBound = true;
  };

  const scan = (root) => {
    if (!root) return;
    root.querySelectorAll?.('a[href]').forEach(hardenAnchor);
    root.querySelectorAll?.('*').forEach((el) => {
      if (el.shadowRoot) {
        try { el.shadowRoot.querySelectorAll('a[href]').forEach(hardenAnchor); } catch {}
        observe(el.shadowRoot);
      }
    });
  };

  const observe = (root) => {
    try {
      const mo = new MutationObserver(() => scan(root));
      mo.observe(root, { childList: true, subtree: true, attributes: true, attributeFilter: ['href'] });
      window.__aiSearchNewTabMOs = window.__aiSearchNewTabMOs || [];
      window.__aiSearchNewTabMOs.push(mo);
    } catch (e) {
      console.warn('[AI_SEARCH:newtab] observer error', e);
    }
  };

  const widget = document.querySelector('gen-search-widget');
  const containers = [widget, document].filter(Boolean);

  containers.forEach((c) => {
    scan(c instanceof Document ? c : (c.shadowRoot || c));
    observe(c instanceof Document ? c : (c.shadowRoot || c));
  });

  if (widget) {
    const tryLate = () => {
      scan(widget);
      if (widget.shadowRoot) scan(widget.shadowRoot);
    };
    setTimeout(tryLate, 250);
    setTimeout(tryLate, 1000);
    setTimeout(tryLate, 2000);
  }

  try { __DBG && __DBG('AI_SEARCH', 'initNewTabEnforcer attached'); } catch {}
}

(function () {

  const DEBUG = /\boasdebug=1\b/i.test(location.search);

  const log = (...a) => DEBUG && console.log('[oas-link]', ...a);

  /* ===== RENDER ===== */
  function renderLoading(loadId) {
    const slot = getSlot();
    if (!slot) return;
    if (slot.querySelector('[data-oas-loading]')?.getAttribute('data-oas-loading') === String(loadId)) return;

  function scheduleFallback(loadId) {

  /* ===== CONTEXT ===== */
  const isInReference = () => location.pathname.includes('/reference/');
  const projectRoot   = () => location.pathname.replace(/\/reference.*/, '');
  const currentSlug   = () => (location.pathname.match(/\/reference\/([^/?#]+)/)||[])[1] || null;

  function readmeVersion() {

    const method = header.querySelector('[data-testid="http-method"]')?.textContent?.trim().toLowerCase() || '';

    const hasUrl   = !!header.querySelector('[data-testid="serverurl"], [data-testid="request-url"]');
    return !!(methodOk && (hasUrl || header.hasAttribute('data-raycast-oas')));

    try { const r = await fetch(url, { method: 'HEAD', credentials: 'include', signal }); return r.ok; }

  const absoluteUrl = (u) => { try { return new URL(u, location.origin).href; } catch { return null; } };

  /* ===== FALLBACK: name-match against /openapi index ===== */
  // Used only when data-raycast-oas is absent. Scores each listed spec by how
  // many tokens from the project root path appear in its filename, then picks
  // the best match without fetching any spec content.
  async function findFromOpenapiIndex(signal) {
    try {
      const res = await fetch(`${projectRoot()}/openapi`, { credentials: 'include', signal });
      if (!res.ok) return null;
      const doc = new DOMParser().parseFromString(await res.text(), 'text/html');
      const links = [...doc.querySelectorAll('a[href$=".json"]')].map(a => a.getAttribute('href')).filter(Boolean);
      const tokens = projectRoot().replace(/^\//, '').split(/[-/]+/).filter(t => t.length > 3);
      const best = links
        .map(href => ({ href, score: tokens.reduce((s, t) => s + (href.toLowerCase().includes(t) ? 1 : 0), 0) }))
        .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)[0];
      if (!best || best.score === 0) return null;
      const filename = best.href.split('/').pop();
      const url = absoluteUrl(`${projectRoot()}/openapi/${filename}`);
      return url ? { url, downloadUrl: url, filename } : null;
    } catch (e) {
      log('/openapi fallback miss:', e.message);
      return null;
    }
  }

  /* ===== WAIT FOR DOM ===== */
  async function waitForHead(timeoutMs = 3000) {
    if (getHead()) return true;
    return new Promise((resolve) => {
      const obs = new MutationObserver(() => { if (getHead()) { obs.disconnect(); resolve(true); } });
      obs.observe(document.documentElement, { childList: true, subtree: true });
      setTimeout(() => { obs.disconnect(); resolve(!!getHead()); }, timeoutMs);
    });
  }

  /* ===== RUN ===== */
  async function run() {
    if (!isInReference()) { moHead.disconnect(); moSide.disconnect(); moHdr.disconnect(); return; }

    if (!getHead()) {
      if (!(await waitForHead(3000))) { scheduleRun('no-head-yet'); return; }
      if (!getHead()) { scheduleRun('no-head-postwait'); return; }
    }

    bindObservers();

    if (!isRealEndpoint()) { removeSlot(); scheduleRun('await-endpoint-hydration'); return; }

    const start = performance.now();
    while (!getH1() && performance.now() - start < 800) await new Promise(r => requestAnimationFrame(r));

    const ver        = readmeVersion() || 'default';
    const slug       = currentSlug() || '';
    const raycastKey = getHeaderRoot()?.getAttribute('data-raycast-oas') || '';
    const ctxKey     = `${ver}::${slug}::${raycastKey}`;
    const slot       = getSlot();

    if (activeCtxKey === ctxKey && currentAbort && !currentAbort.signal.aborted) { log('dedupe: in-flight'); return; }

Configure real-time audiences for Web Experimentation                                                           

The availability of features may depend on your plan type. Contact your Customer Success Manager if you have any questions.

For AI agents: visit https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/llms.txt for an index of all pages formatted in Markdown and endpoints in OpenAPI.

## 

Prerequisites

[](#prerequisites)

*   Have an Optimizely Web Experimentation account.
*   Have an Optimizely Data Platform (ODP) account.
*   [Add the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet to your site](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411731640973).
*   [Add the ODP snippet to your site](https://docs.developers.optimizely.com/optimizely-data-platform/docs/implement-the-odp-javascript-tag).
    
    > 🚧
    > 
    > ### 
    > 
    > Important
    > 
    > [](#important)
    > 
    > The ODP snippet is optional if you select the **Web • Visitor ID** in step 7 below, or if you do not use ODP as your customer data platform (CDP) and are implementing the audience sync version of this integration.
    > 
    > If you add the ODP snippet to your site, it must be before the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet so that the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet can pull the ID that the ODP snippet generates.
    
*   Have [real-time audiences](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/37582243690765-Build-real-time-audiences-in-ODP) configured in ODP.

## 

Integration considerations

[](#integration-considerations)

*   **Third-party CDP** — If you do not use ODP as your CDP, you still need an ODP account but do not have to implement the ODP snippet on your site. To configure the Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation integration using a third-party CDP, skip to [Integrate with other CDPs](#integrate-with-other-cdps).
*   **ODP** — If you use ODP as your CDP, continue to [Configure Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation](#configure-real-time-segments-for-web-experimentation).

## 

Configure Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation

[](#configure-real-time-segments-for-web-experimentation)

1.  Go to **Settings > Integrations > Real-Time Segments** in Optimizely Web Experimentation.
    
    ![Real-Time Segments Integration](https://files.readme.io/b078a0f-real-time_segments_integration.png)
2.  Toggle the integration status to **On**.
    
3.  Click **You can find your API key in ODP** to go to the **APIs** page in ODP.
    
4.  Copy the **KEY** value in the **Public** and **Private** tabs on the **APIs** page in ODP.
    
    ![Copy API Keys](https://files.readme.io/e0c85b0-copy_keys.png)
5.  Go back to Optimizely Web Experimentation and paste these values into the corresponding fields (**ODP Public Key (required)** and **ODP Private Key (required)**).
    
    ![Paste API Keys](https://files.readme.io/5657ab2-Paste_keys.png)
6.  Select your region from the **ODP Host (required)** drop-down list.
    
7.  Select your desired **User ID**:
    
    *   **ODP • VUID** — The ID that ODP assigns to each customer cookie. This is the default ID for the integration.
    *   **Web • Visitor ID** — (Default) The ID that your Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet is using. Depending on your snippet settings, this is either the default Optimizely Web Experimentation visitor ID or [another ID of your choice](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411652974477-Bring-your-own-visitor-ID-BYOID-).
        
        > 🚧
        > 
        > ### 
        > 
        > Important
        > 
        > [](#important-1)
        > 
        > For help with selecting the **User ID**, see [Select your User ID](#select-your-user-id).
        
8.  Select your desired **Confidence Level** for the **User ID** you selected above:
    
    *   **Low confidence** — Low confidence identifiers are unique to a device or browser and may resolve to multiple customers in certain situations. Select this option when there is a weak degree of confidence that your chosen **User ID** accurately represents a single customer.
        
        > 📘
        > 
        > ### 
        > 
        > Note
        > 
        > [](#note)
        > 
        > **Low confidence** is the only option available if you select **ODP • VUID** for your **User ID**.
        
    *   **High confidence** — High confidence identifiers are unique to an individual customer. Select this option only when you have a high degree of confidence that your chosen **User ID** accurately represents a single customer. See [Overview of customer identity and resolution](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4407767067149-Overview-of-customer-identity-and-resolution) for more information.
9.  Click **Save**.
    

### 

Select your User ID

[](#select-your-user-id)

When deciding which **User ID** to select, consider the following requirements for each option:

**ODP • VUID**

*   You must implement both the ODP and Optimizely Web Experimentation snippets on your site.
*   You must have the ODP snippet activated before the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet.
*   You cannot implement the ODP snippet asynchronously.
*   This is a low-confidence identifier.

**Web • Visitor ID**

*   You must implement the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet on your site.
*   Implementing the ODP snippet is optional. If you choose not to implement it, just implement the Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet, then skip directly to [Use ODP real-time segments in your Optimizely Web Experimentation experiments](#use-odp-real-time-segments-in-your-optimizely-web-experimentation-experiments).
*   You can keep your performance budget for your site lower by only implementing one snippet as opposed to implementing both.
*   You can select whether you want this to be a low-confidence or high-confidence identifier.

## 

Integrate with other CDPs

[](#integrate-with-other-cdps)

> 🚧
> 
> ### 
> 
> Important
> 
> [](#important-2)
> 
> If you use ODP as your CDP, do not complete this section. Skip to [Use ODP real-time segments in your Optimizely Web Experimentation experiments](#use-odp-real-time-segments-in-your-optimizely-web-experimentation-experiments).

If you use a third-party CDP:

1.  Configure the [third-party CDP integration in ODP](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/19650895342349-CDP-audience-sync-environment).
2.  Go to **Settings > Integrations > Real-Time Segments** in Optimizely Web Experimentation.
3.  Toggle the integration status to **On**.
4.  Click **You can find your API key in ODP** to navigate to the **APIs** page in ODP.
5.  Copy the **KEY** value in the **Public** and **Private** tabs on the **APIs** page in ODP.
6.  Go back to Optimizely Web Experimentation and paste these values into the corresponding fields (**ODP Public Key (required)** and **ODP Private Key (required)**).
7.  Select your region from the **ODP Host (required)** drop-down list.
8.  Select the **CDP Audience Sync Implementation** checkbox.
9.  Select an **Identifier Type**.
    
    > 🚧
    > 
    > ### 
    > 
    > Important
    > 
    > [](#important-3)
    > 
    > Select an identifier type that matches the identifier sent from your CDP to ODP to increase the likelihood of user bucketing. See [the user documentation on identifier types](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4411652974477-Bring-your-own-visitor-ID-BYOID-#heading-2) for information.
    
10.  Enter the **Identifier Name**.

## 

Use ODP real-time audiences in your Optimizely Web Experimentation experiments

[](#use-odp-real-time-audiences-in-your-optimizely-web-experimentation-experiments)

Now you can build audiences in Optimizely Web Experimentation using ODP's [real-time audiences](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/37582243690765-Build-real-time-audiences-in-ODP).

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> [](#note-1)
> 
> The audiences on the **Customers > Audiences** page in ODP are not available for use in this integration.

### 

Create an audience using ODP's real-time audiences

[](#create-an-audience-using-odps-real-time-audiences)

You can create and add an audience directly in your experiment (described below), or you can create the audience outside of the experiment ([using the audience builder](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/37582243690765-Build-real-time-audiences-in-ODP)) and add it to your experiment later.

1.  Go to **Audiences** in your experiment.
    
2.  Click **Create New Audience**.
    
    ![Create New Audience](https://files.readme.io/d97938c-10f0f4e-odp2-2.png)
3.  Complete the **Name** (required) and **Description** (optional) fields.
    
4.  Expand **Real-Time Segments** in the audience conditions options.
    
5.  Drag and drop either **Custom Segments** to the **Audience Conditions** section.
    
6.  Configure the audience as desired (the real-time segments from ODP display in the **Select an audience** drop-down list).
    
7.  Click **Save Audience**.
    
8.  Click **Save** on the **Audiences** page.
    

> 📘
> 
> ### 
> 
> Note
> 
> [](#note-2)
> 
> The Optimizely Web Experimentation snippet does not evaluate ODP real-time segment membership unless you add an audience that uses ODP real-time audiences to a live experiment that is being activated. Add the audience you create (using the steps above) to an experiment to see this integration function on a particular webpage.
> 
> If you check for a value that could change ODP real-time segment membership mid-session, a page needs to be activated for an experiment using an audience to force re-evaluation (as it normally would for any other audience condition). See [order of activation](https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/4410289779853-How-the-Optimizely-snippet-works-Order-of-activation) for information.

## 

Troubleshoot the integration

[](#troubleshoot-the-integration)

If you do not see the issue you are experiencing below, contact Optimizely Support.

### 

Visitors are not getting bucketed into experiments

[](#visitors-are-not-getting-bucketed-into-experiments)

**API key daily request limit**

In rare cases, you may reach ODP's public API key daily request limit of 1 million. This prevents Web Experimentation from bucketing visitors into experiments that use Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation. Other experiments continue to work, and experiments using Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation resume the next day.

It is unlikely that hitting the ODP public API key daily request limit would cause a sample ratio mismatch (SRM). SRM is related to overall traffic allocation to experiments, not traffic distribution among variations.

If you reach the ODP public API key request limit and the API calls fail for the rest of the day, there may be a slight delay in reaching statistical significance. While the time to the conclusion of a test is driven by an accumulation of evidence, it is _mainly_ driven by an accumulation of evidence where there is a consistent, compelling effect to be found. What impacts the speed to a conclusion is more about a thoughtfully designed experiment.

**ID not found**

You may see a message from ODP that it could not locate a visitor's ID to bucket them. This is not bad and is a possibility in the integration due to what is called a [race condition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_condition).

When the snippet activates, it evaluates the URL targeting in the project. When the page's targeting conditions are passed, the page activates, and Optimizely Web Experimentation evaluates the experiments for that page and whether a visitor should be in the experiment, based on traffic allocation and audience conditions. If both audience and traffic conditions are passed, the experiment activates.

During bucketing, Optimizely Web Experimentation generates a random ID for the user and sets it as a cookie while activating the snippet. With Real-Time Segments, Optimizely Web Experimentation calls ODP to retrieve the segments for the visitor's ID. If the snippet asks for the ID before the ID has reached ODP, ODP may give an unrecognized ID response because sending data to ODP is slower than the snipper activation. This is called a race condition, where the end result differs based on the order in which concurrent logic is completed.

After receiving this response from ODP, Optimizely Web Experimentation does not attempt to finish bucketing for that experiment or campaign and moves to the next experience.

**Network request interception**

When an experiment targets Real-Time Segments from ODP, Web Experimentation uses the GraphQL API from ODP to fetch the visitor's RTS membership. As with any other third-party audience integrations, Web Experimentation waits for a response for a maximum of 2 seconds. If the API response does not return within 2 seconds, the audience is evaluated as false, and the visitor is not bucketed into the experiment.

On some websites, your JavaScript framework may intercept the network requests that Web Experimentation initiates. This interception adds overhead and can delay the network request and response, causing Web Experimentation to receive the response from ODP after 2 seconds.

To prevent this, Optimizely Support can enable sandboxing in the Web Experimentation project. This is a project-level setting not directly accessible to you. When enabled, the snippet adds an empty iframe to the `<head>` section of your website. The API requests to third-party audience integrations are then passed through that iframe, which should prevent them from being intercepted. This lets the responses get back to Web Experimentation in time to evaluate the audiences correctly.

To see if this issue is occurring, open **Developer tools > Network**. Filter the network logs for **graphql**, and select the **Initiator** tab. The initiator stack should show the snippet. If the stack shows another script, this indicates the request from the snippet was intercepted, and delays may occur. Contact the Support team for further investigation and possible enabling of the Sandboxing setting.

### 

Check which real-time audiences you are assigned to in ODP

[](#check-which-real-time-audiences-you-are-assigned-to-in-odp)

When Real-Time Segments for Web Experimentation is enabled, Optimizely Web Experimentation makes a request to the ODP GraphQL API to retrieve the current visitor's assigned real-time audiences. To inspect the data returned by that call, open the developer console and check the value of this attribute:

JavaScript

`   window["optimizely"].get("visitor")['vendor.odp']['audiences']   `

The content of this array should be populated with any real-time segments to which you are currently assigned.

If you do not see any real-time audiences in the `odp.audiences[]` array, first check to see if you are a member of the `returning_visitors` real-time segment by navigating away from the page and returning to it. If you see yourself in the `returning_visitors` real-time audience on your second visit to the page, the problem could be that you do not belong to any other audiences, or those audiences have not been enabled for that page.

If, however, you are _not_ in the `returning_visitors` real-time segment, the ODP tracker may be disabled. This often happens when a visitor deletes their browser cookies mid-session. In this case, the ODP tracker needs to reacquire a tracking cookie before it can identify the user. If the ODP JavaScript snippet cannot find the cookie, ODP returns an empty array of audience memberships. You can reset the cookie by logging out and back into the site.
